title: Wigner negativity costs phase-space area: A conjectured refinement of the Lieb–Solovej inequality at Rényi order one half
problem: The Husimi function \(Q\) of a light mode is a genuine probability density, the outcome distribution of heterodyne detection, and the Lieb–Solovej theorem says no state concentrates it more than a coherent state does. The Wigner function \(W\) can be negative, and its negativity is a resource that sets the cost of simulating the state classically. The Lieb–Solovej bound says a state cannot be narrower than a coherent state, but not how much wider a nonclassical state must be. Does Wigner negativity force a quantifiable spread of the Husimi function?
result: The paper conjectures that \(\ln\|W\|_1\le h_{1/2}(Q)-\ln(8\pi)\) for every single-mode state, where \(h_{1/2}\) is the Rényi entropy of order one half and equality holds only for coherent states. It proves that pure states suffice, proves the inequality for all states with the weaker constant \(\ln(4\pi)\), and shows that no argument treating the Wigner function as a generic two-mode wavefunction can do better. It also shows that the analogous statement fails for the Wehrl entropy and higher Rényi orders, so the conjecture does not follow from majorization.
significance: If true, the conjecture refines a classic inequality of phase-space analysis with a remainder that is an operational resource. It would let heterodyne statistics alone certify an upper bound on Wigner negativity, and hence on the overhead \(\|W\|_1^2\) of quasi-probability simulation, without tomography. The analysis pinpoints where existing proofs lose the factor of two: interference in the Wigner function, which any proof must retain.
limitations: The main statement is a conjecture, supported by numerical tests on random superpositions of up to eight Fock states and by the proven weaker bound, which improves on Lieb–Solovej only when \(\|W\|_1>2\). The right-hand side is not invariant under squeezing, so the bound is tightest after choosing the best general-dyne measurement. The work covers one mode; the multimode version is open. The author acknowledges the use of Claude Opus 5.5 in building and debugging the code for the numerical section.
summary_basis: Description based on the full arXiv HTML of v1, read 2026-11-25: Secs. I–VII and the acknowledgements; Appendices A–D were not read. Editorial checks: for Fock states n = 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 40 the computed values of ln‖W‖₁ are 0.355, 0.548, 0.681, 0.869, 1.148, 1.449, 1.765 and the Rényi-1/2 excesses are 0.452, 0.693, 0.857, 1.080, 1.402, 1.736, 2.077, so the conjecture holds with margin. For the superposition |0⟩ + 0.2|β⟩ centred at (6, 0), a grid computation gave ‖W‖₁ = 1.2270 and entropy excesses 0.304, 0.161, 0.077, 0.039 at orders 1/2, 1, 2, ∞, reproducing the paper's table.

methods_basis: Based on the linked paper version. Derivations marked as editorial, and suggested uses in other problems, are editorial guidance rather than results of the paper.
description: With \(\hbar=1\) and phase-space point \(\mathbf r=(x,p)\), the Husimi function is \(Q(\mathbf r)=\langle\mathbf r|\rho|\mathbf r\rangle/2\pi\), the probability density of heterodyne outcomes. Its Rényi entropy of order one half is \(h_{1/2}(Q)=2\ln\int\sqrt Q\), whose exponential is an effective phase-space area, \(8\pi\) for a coherent state. The Wigner function has \(\|W\|_1=\int|W|\ge1\), with equality exactly when \(W\ge0\); the Wigner logarithmic negativity \(\ln\|W\|_1\) is a monotone in the resource theory of non-Gaussianity.

The conjecture reads \(\|W\|_1\le(\int\sqrt Q)^2/8\pi\): negativity is at most the area a state occupies in units of the coherent-state area. For Wigner-positive states it reduces to the Lieb–Solovej bound \(h_{1/2}(Q)\ge\ln(8\pi)\). Because the left side is convex in the state and the right side is concave, the gap is convex and violations, if any, must occur at pure states. Thousands of random pure states, including near-vacuum superpositions where the gap tends to zero, showed none.

Writing \(W\) through the coherent-state resolution of the identity and applying the triangle and Cauchy–Schwarz inequalities proves the bound with \(4\pi\) in place of \(8\pi\). For pure states the only loss is the triangle inequality, which discards the phase that makes the Wigner function oscillate. For the vacuum, the bound \(e^{-r^2/2}/\pi\) replaces the true \(e^{-r^2}/\pi\), and integrated over phase space this is exactly the factor of two.

A structural argument explains why the factor is hard to recover. For a pure state, \(W\) is, up to scaling, the position wavefunction of a two-mode state made from \(\bar\psi\otimes\psi\) by passive optics, and \(\int\sqrt Q\) is the coherent-state \(L^1\) norm of that state. Over arbitrary two-mode wavefunctions the weaker constant is optimal, as products of squeezed vacua show, so a sharp proof must use the product structure. A dilute superposition of the vacuum with a distant coherent state satisfies the conjecture but violates its analogues at orders 1, 2 and \(\infty\), because the negativity responds at first order in the small amplitude while those entropies respond only at second order.

methods.technique: Reduction to pure states by convexity against concavity
methods.explanation: The negativity side is a norm of a linear function of the state, hence convex. The area side is the square of an integral of \(\sqrt Q\), and a Cauchy–Schwarz argument shows it is concave. Their difference is convex, so it is largest at extreme points.
math: Let \(\rho=\sum_kp_k\rho_k\) with pure \(\rho_k\), and \(M(\rho)=\int\sqrt{Q_\rho}\). The triangle inequality gives \(\|W_\rho\|_1\le\sum_kp_k\|W_{\rho_k}\|_1\). For the other side, \[M(\rho_k)^2=\Bigl(\int\frac{\sqrt{Q_{\rho_k}}}{Q_\rho^{1/4}}\,Q_\rho^{1/4}\Bigr)^2\le\int\frac{Q_{\rho_k}}{\sqrt{Q_\rho}}\int\sqrt{Q_\rho}.\]

Multiplying by \(p_k\), summing and using \(\sum_kp_kQ_{\rho_k}=Q_\rho\) gives \(\sum_kp_kM(\rho_k)^2\le M(\rho)^2\). If the conjecture holds for each \(\rho_k\), then \[\|W_\rho\|_1\le\sum_kp_k\|W_{\rho_k}\|_1\le\frac{1}{8\pi}\sum_kp_kM(\rho_k)^2\le\frac{1}{8\pi}M(\rho)^2.\] Equality would need \(Q_{\rho_k}=Q_\rho\) for all \(k\), hence a pure state, so mixed states satisfy the bound strictly.

Editorial check on Fock states, where both sides have closed forms: \(W_n\propto(-1)^nL_n(2r^2)e^{-r^2}\) and \(Q_n\propto e^{-r^2/2}(r^2/2)^n/n!\). Numerically, \(\ln\|W\|_1\) is 0.355 against an entropy excess of 0.452 at \(n=1\), and 1.765 against 2.077 at \(n=40\): the conjecture holds with a margin that grows slowly with \(n\).
methods.transfer: Pairing a convex resource measure with a concave functional of an observable distribution reduces any such inequality to pure states. The same Cauchy–Schwarz step shows concavity of \((\int p^{1/2})^2\) for any linear family of densities.

methods.technique: A coherent-state bound and the interference it discards
methods.explanation: Expanding the parity operator in coherent states writes \(W\) as an integral of off-diagonal coherent-state matrix elements with an oscillating phase. Dropping the phase and bounding each element by Cauchy–Schwarz gives a product of square roots of \(Q\), which integrates to \((\int\sqrt Q)^2\), with a factor of two lost to the dropped interference.
math: Using \(\hat\Pi\ket{\mathbf s}=\ket{-\mathbf s}\) and the coherent-state resolution of the identity, \[W(\mathbf r)=\frac1\pi\int\frac{d^2\mathbf s}{2\pi}\,e^{i(xs_p-ps_x)}\langle\mathbf r+\mathbf s|\rho|\mathbf r-\mathbf s\rangle.\] Since \(|\langle\mathbf u|\rho|\mathbf v\rangle|\le2\pi\sqrt{Q(\mathbf u)Q(\mathbf v)}\), dropping the phase gives \(|W(\mathbf r)|\le\frac1\pi\int d^2\mathbf s\sqrt{Q(\mathbf r+\mathbf s)Q(\mathbf r-\mathbf s)}\). Changing variables to \(\mathbf u=\mathbf r+\mathbf s\), \(\mathbf v=\mathbf r-\mathbf s\) (Jacobian \(1/4\)) factorizes the double integral: \(\|W\|_1\le(\int\sqrt Q)^2/4\pi\).

For pure states the Cauchy–Schwarz step is an equality, so the entire loss is the phase. For the vacuum the bound \(e^{-r^2/2}/\pi\) is tight only at the origin; elsewhere the phase \(e^{i(xs_p-ps_x)}\) oscillates and halves the decay rate of \(W\), which after integration is the factor between \(4\pi\) and \(8\pi\).

The same calculation shows why order one half is special. For \(\ket0+t\ket\beta\) with \(\beta\) far away, interference fringes contribute negativity of order \(t\), while \(\int Q^\alpha\) changes at order \(t^{2\alpha}\); only at \(\alpha=1/2\) do both respond linearly. Editorial check: with \(t=0.2\) and the coherent state centred at \((6,0)\), \(\ln\|W\|_1=0.205\), while the entropy excesses are 0.304, 0.161, 0.077 and 0.039 at orders \(1/2\), 1, 2 and \(\infty\), as in the paper's table.
methods.transfer: Bounding a quasi-probability through coherent-state matrix elements, and identifying exactly which phase the bound discards, is a template for comparing other phase-space functionals, such as Kirkwood–Dirac or discrete Wigner negativities, with entropies of measured distributions.
